cases.title: The Pull of the First Patient
cases.presentation: You arrive first at a bus vs. truck collision. A screaming woman with an open femur fracture is right by your door. Through the windshield you see at least 20 more people, some not moving.
cases.question: What do you do?
options: A: Splint the femur — she's right here.
C: Partner does a quick recon/global sort while you declare MCI, name command, and send METHANE.
D: Load her and transport to clear the scene.
cases.explanation: First-in doesn't get sucked in. The open femur can wait seconds; the scene can't run without command. Declare, report, request, then assign triage.
cases.clinicalPearl: Your first radio transmission is the most valuable intervention you'll do all day.

cases.title: Build the METHANE
cases.presentation: Gas explosion in a 3-story restaurant at 42 Harbor Rd, rear wall collapsed, smell of gas still present. Approx 15 casualties: 3 critical, 5 serious, 7 walking. Harbor Rd blocked by debris; access via Mill Lane. Your unit and one engine on scene.
cases.question: Which report is BEST?
options: B: 'Explosion at Harbor Rd, lots hurt, will update.'

D: 'Major incident declared. 42 Harbor Rd, rear of restaurant. Gas explosion with partial collapse. Hazards: ongoing gas leak, unstable structure. Access via Mill Lane — Harbor Rd blocked. Approx 15: 3 red, 5 yellow, 7 green. On scene: 1 ambulance, 1 engine; request 6 ambulances, USAR, gas utility, police.'
cases.explanation: This hits every METHANE element in one concise transmission, including the critical hazard (gas) and the access change (Mill Lane).
cases.clinicalPearl: If you can't remember METHANE, read it off the action card on your visor.

cases.title: Quiet Lobby
cases.presentation: Dispatch: 'multiple people fainted in a subway station.' On arrival you see commuters coughing as they exit, several collapsed on the platform stairs, and pigeons dead near a vent.
cases.question: Best action?
options: A: Bring the patients to your ambulance immediately.
B: Stop, withdraw upwind, keep ambulatory exiting patients in one area, report suspected chemical MCI (METHANE) and request HazMat/decon.
C: Enter with a BVM and start triage.
cases.explanation: Multiple collapsed casualties without trauma + dead animals = chemical clues. Don't approach (Step 1-2-3), control the exiting crowd for decon, and report.
cases.clinicalPearl: Dead birds and fallen people — don't be the next one down.
